headline: Super Troopers top the week; Aeil steals one by a whisker
lede: Week 2 came in loud, pardner: 143.89 at the top of the ledger, 66.21 at the bottom, and a pair of finishes decided by less ground than a hired hand could spit across. Three outfits are rollin' unbeaten and three ain't found the trail yet. And somewhere in the middle, a 35.69 quarterback sat on the bench watchin' the wagon burn.
paragraphs: Warthogs rode right over Norskes U Betcha, 122.9 to 68.38, the widest margin anybody posted this week at 54.52. Devin Lloyd put up 27.0 at linebacker, best defensive day in the whole territory, while Courtland Sutton chipped in a lonesome 2.45. Norskes U Betcha left Tyler Shough and his 28.39 sittin' by the campfire; a better lineup was worth 23.01, which still wouldn't have closed that canyon. Both wagons sit at 1-1.

densmen struck the vein for 141.48 and buried Jack Attack's 96.06 by 45.42, with the Patriots defense hauling in 34.0 all by itself. Jack Attack had Josh Allen go off for 42.01 and still lost, on account of Patrick Mahomes and his 35.69 never leaving the bench: worst lineup in the league this week, worth 33.3 more points properly arranged. DJ Moore's 0.15 didn't help the cause neither. Both outfits are 1-1.

Long Howie stays unbeaten at 2-0, takin' Jrod 107.84 to 66.21, a 41.63 walk in the sunshine. Jared Goff did the heavy haulin' with 36.49, and Long Howie set the cleanest table in the league: a better lineup was worth all of 0.3. Jrod posted the low score of the week and left TreVeyon Henderson's 14.0 on the bench, with 18.45 available for the askin'.

Justin's Bad Team is not, in fact, a bad team this week: 123.01 over sisu's 96.41 by 26.6, with the Panthers defense stampeding to 38.0. Marvin Harrison Jr. turned in a clean 0.0 and it didn't even matter, though 23.9 more was sittin' there with Tre Tucker's 14.95 on the bench. sisu got 17.06 from Bo Nix and not much of a posse behind him. Both ride out at 1-1.

Super Troopers claimed the high score of the week at 143.89 and held off HAWKSRULE's 121.78 by 22.11, which is a real shootout by any measure. Brock Purdy led the charge with 30.44 for the winners, who are now 2-0. HAWKSRULE got a fine 34.35 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba, put up the 3rd best pile of points in the league, and still walks home 0-2. Hard luck, and that's the honest word for it.

Scott's Hype rode the Vikings defense and its 30.0 to 111.59, enough to handle WeBleedOrangeAndBlue's 90.49 by 21.1. Scott's Hype left near nothing on the table, just 1.7 worth of better arranging. WeBleedOrangeAndBlue had Bryce Young and his 25.84 parked on the bench while Joe Burrow's 19.09 led the starters, a 17.1 mistake that drops them to 0-2.

Zihuatanejo survived Dart Star Orchestra by 1.9, 99.3 to 97.4, and stays unbeaten at 2-0. CeeDee Lamb's 27.85 carried the water, which was needed since the Lions defense turned in 0.0. Dart Star Orchestra had 24.59 sittin' in better arrangements, including the Jets defense and its 14.0 on the bench, while Jaxson Dart managed 1.2 as a starter. That one stung, and it'll sting a while.

Closest race in the territory: Aeil edged e-mans revenge by 1.08, 123.42 to 122.34. James Cook III went for 22.55 for Aeil, who somehow won with Drew Lock's 23.9 gathering dust on the bench and 14.53 available in a better lineup. e-mans revenge got a stout 33.29 from Matthew Stafford, left 19.5 on the table, and falls to 0-2 by less than the width of a horseshoe nail.
sign_off: 11 weeks left in the regular season and 8 seats by the fire when it's done. Plenty of trail yet, so check your lineups before you check your mail.
purse: Commissioner's purse pays 4 deep this week: Super Troopers takes the $40 top prize on 143.89, densmen collects $20 on 141.48, Aeil banks $10 on 123.42, and Justin's Bad Team squeaks into the money for $5 on 123.01. That's 2 weeks in the money already for densmen, and a first taste for the other 3.
